transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
Hello, Dr. Smith. Lately, I've been losing a lot of weight and I'm barely eating anything. I'm only managing to eat extremely small amounts of food each day.
Are you intentionally restricting your food intake due to fear of gaining weight or body image concerns?
Yes, I've been skipping meals and strictly limiting my food because I'm terrified of gaining weight. Even though I've lost weight, when I look in the mirror, I still feel so fat.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Anorexia Nervosa", "Major Depressive Disorder", "Persistent Depressive Disorder", "Bulimia Nervosa", "Binge-Eating Disorder"], but based on this conversation, the patient endorses intentional food restriction due to fear of weight gain and distorted body image (feeling fat despite weight loss), which are core diagnostic features of Anorexia Nervosa. Bulimia Nervosa and Binge-Eating Disorder are ruled out due to absence of bingeing or purging behaviors. Major Depressive Disorder and Persistent Depressive Disorder are less likely because mood symptoms were not reported and the primary disturbance appears to be around eating and body image. Thus, the current candidate is exclusively Anorexia Nervosa.
